# Guidance

When you begin work on a new feature you should always take the time to carefully think about the full end-to-end lifecycle of the change including how it will be discovered by the various stakeholders across engineering and product and support and how each of them will interact with the change during its rollout and steady state operation, taking into account all of the runbooks and observability dashboards and paging integrations that might need to be updated in parallel to keep the operational surface consistent with the intended behavior after the change ships, because otherwise you risk introducing an invisible gap in operational readiness that a future on-call engineer will discover at 3am when the paging system fires without enough context to resolve the incident, and that is a strictly worse outcome for the team than taking a few extra hours during planning to enumerate the operational touch points and validate them with the relevant owners before writing any production code, especially given how tightly coupled many of our systems have become since the last platform migration and how many of the old assumptions embedded in our tooling are no longer valid in the current architecture.
